title: Morphisms in $D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ descend to a finite extension
statement:
Let $X$ be a standing scheme, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite and $C,D\in\Dbc(X,E)$. For finite
$F\supseteq E$ and every $r\in\mathbf Z$:

1. $\Hom_{D(X,F)}(C_F,D_F[r])\cong\Hom_{D(X,E)}(C,\operatorname{Res}D_F[r])$, and likewise over $\Qlb$,
   naturally in $F$;
2. if $D^\bullet$ is a bounded complex representing $D$, then $(D^\bullet\otimes_{E_X}F_X)_F$ is a
   filtered system of complexes of $E_X$-modules vanishing below the lower bound of $D^\bullet$,
   with colimit $D^\bullet\otimes_{E_X}\QbarX$;
3. the map $\varinjlim_F\Hom(C_F,D_F[r])\to\Hom(C_{\Qlb},D_{\Qlb}[r])$ is bijective.

proof.text: Work on a small skeleton of $X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$ in a universe containing the coefficient diagram, and put $R=E_X$. The ambient abelian sheaf tensor is closed symmetric monoidal and preserves colimits [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Thus [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] gives $B\otimes_R-\dashv U_B$, for $B=F_X$ or $\QbarX$, with exact restriction $U_B$. Extension is right exact by that same statement and preserves finite limits by [lem-sfb-subfield-flat] or [lem-sfb-qlbar-flat]; hence it is exact.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy](a) to this additive adjunction to get the adjunction on complexes. Both termwise functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Apply [lem-sfb-adjunction-localization] to the derived localization functors. This gives the derived adjunction with $\alpha_B(f)=U_B(f)\circ\eta_C^B$, where $\eta_M^B(m)=1\otimes m$, and inverse $g\mapsto\epsilon\circ(B\otimes_R g)$, where $\epsilon(b\otimes n)=bn$. Restriction commutes with shifts by the exact-functor shift comparison.

source.place: paragraph (1): localization of the unit and counit

proof.text: The functors $T_{E,F}$ and $T_{E,\Qlb}$ in [def-sfb-derived-extend-subfield] and [def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar] are left-derived extensions. By the exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], they identify naturally with the termwise extensions just used; the same holds for intermediate coefficient fields. Transporting the adjunction along these comparisons proves clause (1) for the functors in the statement, with $U_B(D_B[r])=(U_BD_B)[r]$.

source.place: paragraph (1): identify the chosen derived extensions

proof.text: For $B\to B'$ induced by $F\subseteq F'$ or $F\subseteq\Qlb$, the balanced maps $b'\otimes(b\otimes m)\mapsto b'i(b)\otimes m$ and $b'\otimes m\mapsto b'\otimes(1\otimes m)$ are inverse, giving $B'\otimes_B(B\otimes_R M)\cong B'\otimes_R M$. They commute with differentials. They carry the composite unit $m\mapsto1\otimes(1\otimes m)$ to $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. The equal-right-adjoint uniqueness of [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] identifies this map with the unit-compatible scalar comparison underlying [def-sfb-derived-extend-comp-iso]. Thus $f\mapsto f_{B'}$ here is the actual extension map $\theta_{D[r]}\circ T_{F,B'}(f)\circ\theta_C^{-1}$ used in clause (3).

source.place: paragraph (1): tensor transitivity and the canonical comparison

proof.text: Put $t_M:B\otimes_RM\to B'\otimes_RM$, $b\otimes m\mapsto i(b)\otimes m$. Then $t_C\circ\eta_C^B=\eta_C^{B'}$. Naturality of the $B\to B'$ unit, on complexes and then after localization, gives $U_{B'}(f_{B'})\circ t_C=t_{D[r]}\circ U_B(f)$. Substituting into the Hom formula of step 2 yields $\alpha_{B'}(f_{B'})=t_{D[r]}\circ\alpha_B(f)$. This proves naturality in the coefficient field and identifies all maps to $\Qlb$ as well.

Let $I$ be the set of finite subfields $F\subseteq\Qlb$ containing $E$. It contains $E$ and is directed by finite composita [det-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed-subextensions]. The ring colimit [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x] remains $\QbarX$ when restricted to $I$: extend a cocone on $I$ to every finite $H$ by $H_X\to(EH)_X$ followed by its cocone map. For $H\subseteq H'$ compatibility holds in $(EH')_X$, and restriction and extension of cocones are inverse. All legs are the specified inclusion-induced coefficient maps.

source.place: paragraph (2): the index and its coefficient colimit

proof.text: For use as $R$-modules, identify internal modules in tensor abelian sheaves with sectionwise module sheaves by [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Its hypotheses hold on the chosen small site: abelian sheafification and its strong monoidal tensor comparison are supplied by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Apply [lem-sfb-directed-ring-sheaf-module-colimit] with $A_F=F_X$, $A=\QbarX$, and $s_F:R\to F_X$ the inclusions. The ring cocone was established in step 6, and $q_Fs_F$ is the same inclusion $R\to\QbarX$. Its conclusion says that this very cocone is the colimit in $R$-modules. Transport through the equivalence preserves that universal property.

By [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits], tensoring sectionwise module sheaves with a fixed $M$ preserves this coefficient-sized colimit. Under the equivalence of step 7 this tensor is the internal relative tensor: its two parallel maps are precisely the balancing maps in [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor], so both represent balanced bilinear morphisms. Hence $\varinjlim_{F\in I}(F_X\otimes_RM)\cong\QbarX\otimes_RM$, with the canonical tensor cocone. For $M=D^n$, the differential is $b\otimes m\mapsto b\otimes d(m)$, so these comparisons commute with differentials. If $D^n=0$ below $a$, then all the stage tensors are zero there. This proves clause (2).

source.place: paragraph (2): commute tensor and colimit degreewise

proof.text: The standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] makes $X$ finite type over a field $k$. A field has only the ideals $0$ and $k$, and its spectrum is a single quasi-compact point; thus $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to conclude that $X$ is Noetherian. By [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], choose $a\le b$ outside which $H^i(D)=0$. Apply [lem-sfb-bounded-representative] to the abelian category of $E_X$-module objects to choose $D^\bullet$ representing $D$ and zero outside $[a,b]$.

source.place: paragraph (3): Noetherian hypothesis and bounded representative

proof.text: Let $K_F^\bullet=F_X\otimes_{E_X}D^\bullet$, restricted to $E_X$-modules. Steps 6–8 give a small filtered diagram with common lower bound $a$ and termwise colimit $\QbarX\otimes_{E_X}D^\bullet$. Steps 1–3 identify these with $U_FD_F$ and $U_{\Qlb}D_{\Qlb}$. The theorem [sk-lem-constructible-ext-continuity] explicitly covers every $C\in\Dbc(X,E)$; its scheme hypothesis holds by step 9. Apply it with $\Lambda=\underline E$ and $q=r$. It makes $\varinjlim_F\Hom_{D(X,E)}(C,K_F^\bullet[r])\to\Hom_{D(X,E)}(C,(\QbarX\otimes_{E_X}D^\bullet)[r])$ bijective. The identity in step 5 identifies both the source diagram and every cocone leg with the specified coefficient-extension Hom diagram. Consequently this bijection is exactly the map in clause (3).

source.place: paragraph (3): Ext continuity and its canonical map
